title: Rock, rhythm and blues and Smiling Joe
summary: Rock fading, rhythm and blues returning, and Joe Robichaux's talent.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well, it's on its way out now. I understand the biggest discotheque in, uh, New York called Arthur. They're for sale. And these things are dying on the street. There aren't too many of them left anyway, thank God, because with that, uh, amplification was too much. Too much. I mean, they weren't content with you hearing the music. They had to, you know, just actually beat your eardrums in with it. I don't know how they stand it. But it's on its way out. Now the thing seems to be too a little, uh, the folk has gone somewhat waned in popularity. Now it's the rhythm and blues thing that's come back. What we did was Smiling Joe up there, and Joe Robichaud and Lizzie Miles and Blanche Thomas did up there. But we always did the blues for New Orleans and rhythm and blues. And Joe was another one that should have gone ahead and made himself a million dollars, because he is one of the most talented bluesmen, you know. Do you know Smiling Joe? Yes, I know.
He used to play the guitar.
Now he's just fooling with the piano a little bit.
Yeah, he plays up there on the 600 blocks.
